choices.text: A test of homogeneity, with df = 4.
choices.rationale: Homogeneity applies to separate samples from different populations, and here there is one sample.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = 9.
choices.rationale: Used rows times columns instead of (rows - 1)(columns - 1) for the degrees of freedom.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = 3.
choices.rationale: Used the number of categories minus 1 for one variable only.

title: Homogeneity or independence, and degrees of freedom (variant 2)
stem: A health researcher takes independent random samples of 100 patients from each of two clinics and records whether each patient's outcome is improved, unchanged or worse. The researcher wants to know whether the distribution of outcomes is the same at the two clinics. Which test and degrees of freedom are correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = 2.
choices.rationale: Independence applies to one sample classified on two variables.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A test of homogeneity, with df = 5.
choices.rationale: Used the number of cells minus 1, which is the degrees of freedom for a goodness-of-fit test, not for a two-way table.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A test of homogeneity, with df = (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2.
choices.rationale: Correct: separate samples from two populations gives homogeneity; df = 1 x 2 = 2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A test of homogeneity, with df = 1.
choices.rationale: Used the number of clinics minus 1 only.

title: Homogeneity or independence, and degrees of freedom (variant 3)
stem: A random sample of 300 students is classified by grade level (freshman, sophomore, junior, senior) and by whether the student owns a car (yes or no). The researcher wants to know whether grade level and car ownership are related. Which test and degrees of freedom are correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = (4 - 1)(2 - 1) = 3.
choices.rationale: Correct: one sample classified on two variables gives independence; df = 3 x 1 = 3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = 8.
choices.rationale: Used rows times columns instead of (rows - 1)(columns - 1) for the degrees of freedom.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A test of homogeneity, with df = 3.
choices.rationale: Homogeneity applies to separate samples from different populations, and here there is one sample.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A test of independence, with df = 5.
choices.rationale: Added the numbers of rows and columns minus 1.

title: Expected counts and chi-square conditions (variant 1)
stem: A random sample of 100 people was classified by group and response. Group 1 (40 people): 4 responded yes and 36 responded no. Group 2 (60 people): 16 responded yes and 44 responded no. A researcher plans a chi-square test. Which statement about the conditions is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The expected counts condition is met, because every expected count is at least 5; the smallest is 40(20)/100 = 8.
choices.rationale: Correct: column totals 20 and 80; expected counts: 8, 32, 12, 48.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The conditions are not met, because the observed count of 4 is less than 5.
choices.rationale: The condition applies to expected counts, and an observed count below 5 does not violate it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The conditions are not met, because the two groups are not the same size.
choices.rationale: Groups of different sizes do not violate any condition, because the check is on expected counts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The expected counts condition is met, because the observed counts add to 100.
choices.rationale: The total being 100 does not by itself guarantee every expected count is at least 5.

title: Expected counts and chi-square conditions (variant 2)
stem: A chi-square test of independence is planned for a random sample of 200 people classified in a 3 x 3 table. The row totals are 30, 50 and 120, and the column totals are 10, 90 and 100. Which statement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The expected counts condition is met, because the sample size of 200 is large.
choices.rationale: The total sample size does not guarantee that every expected count is large.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The expected counts condition is met, because every row total is at least 30.
choices.rationale: The condition is about expected counts in every cell, not row totals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The expected counts condition is not met, because some expected counts are less than 5; for example, 30(10)/200 = 1.5.
choices.rationale: Correct: expected count for row 1, column 1 = 1.5 < 5; row 2, column 1 = 2.5.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The expected counts condition is not met, because the column totals are not equal.
choices.rationale: Unequal column totals do not violate the condition, because the check is on each expected count.

title: Expected counts and chi-square conditions (variant 3)
stem: A chi-square test of independence on a 3 x 3 table gives a test statistic of 11.5. For a chi-square distribution with 4 degrees of freedom, P(chi-square > 9.49) = 0.05 and P(chi-square > 13.28) = 0.01. Which conclusion is correct at alpha = 0.05?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reject H0, because 11.5 is greater than 9.49; the p-value is between 0.01 and 0.05, so there is convincing evidence of an association.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fail to reject H0, because 11.5 is less than 13.28.
choices.rationale: Compared with the critical value for 0.01 instead of alpha = 0.05.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reject H0, because the test statistic is greater than 4, the number of degrees of freedom.
choices.rationale: The comparison is with a critical value or p-value, not with the degrees of freedom.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reject H0, because 11.5 proves that the two variables are related by cause and effect.
choices.rationale: A significant association does not establish cause and effect.
